symptom: `mxcli layout flows` on a flow whose loop had been written by the pre-#1935 builder kept the stale loop Size (e.g. 710;480 where the body fits 320;160): it reported `moved 4 of 5 objects` while bson dump showed the Size unchanged, and a later --dry-run reported the same objects as needing to move again.
cause: Two independent carries. (1) stripFlowLayout cleared @position/@anchor/@curve/@merge/@start but not @size, so DESCRIBE re-emitted the STORED loop box and the rebuild reused it verbatim. (2) canon.CarryUnexpressed/carryLoopSize takes max(written, stored) per dimension on every write (the #2179 contract, when MDL could not state a size), so even the correct smaller box was replaced by the larger stored one before equality, eliding the write as unchanged. Measured: writing Size=320;160 directly through UpdateRawUnit read back 710;480.
fix: stripFlowLayout now also clears ActivityAnnotations.Size so the rebuild's fitContainerSize decides. Added canon.ContentsOwnLayout() to skip the loop-size carry when the caller owns the layout, and a backend write path UpdateRawUnitOwningLayout (interface, modelsdk backend, writer, mock, regenerated unimplemented/unsupported) that layoutFlow uses. Tests: mdl/executor/issue1935_layout_flows_test.go (inject stale Size, layout must replace it, second run unchanged) and canon TestUnexpressed_LoopSizeReplacingStaleBoxWhenLayoutOwnsIt, with the #2179 default-carry tests as the control.
insight: Two carry rules can stack: an unexpressed-state carry (canon) and a 'describe it back' annotation each restore a value the command just fixed, and elision then makes the run look clean while the write never lands. To tell them apart, write the intended bytes directly through UpdateRawUnit and read back: reverting means the carry is in canon, surviving means the describe/strip path. A write path authoritative about geometry needs an explicit canon option, not a largest-dimension heuristic.
